title: Types of friction (ঘর্ষণের প্রকারভেদ)
placement: Book pages 89–90, topic 3.9.1: ঘর্ষণের প্রকারভেদ (Types of Friction): স্থিতি, গতি ও আবর্ত ঘর্ষণ. Next to the three definitions with fₛ = μₛN and fₖ = μₖN, and the rolling-friction paragraph (suitcase wheels).
description: Vivid 3D comparison of static, kinetic and rolling friction for textbook topic 3.9.1, pages 89–90. A human with connected anatomical clothing and limbs pushes the same hollow 2 kg crate directly on the floor, then pushes its loaded wheeled trolley by a real handle. The hands follow the contact and stance shoes stay planted while walking. Orange push, red friction and blue velocity arrows follow the original physics: static friction matches 3, 6 and 9 N pushes, sliding friction is 7.84 N, and rolling resistance 0.98 N. Both rolling-force arrows are explicitly magnified 3× for visibility; values stay in newtons. A live force/motion panel, pause control and separate force-direction/formula pages distinguish speeding up, constant speed and slowing down, including why balanced forces keep an already-moving box moving. The separate formula page explains the static limit. Five existing scene-based questions remain, with arrow readouts replacing the force meter. The current human/crate/trolley and vectors export as GLB. Offline in Bangla and English.
